answer: A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The knoll cap is upheld at intake and beacon makes public the per-origin counts. At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a copper tag. That is 21 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
